newsitem.title: RUSSIA: World Bank could lend Russia more if deal right.
newsitem.headline: World Bank could lend Russia more if deal right.

text.p: The World Bank is prepared to make new loans to Russia to support economic reform and social protection, but more must be done to implement existing programmes, senior official Caio Koch-Weser said on Friday.

Koch-Weser, managing director operations, said he had told Russian leaders the bank was willing to expand its activities, through lending and other services, to areas such as the social sector, agriculture and the environment.

"There is a real option when the government considers its borrowing requirement, domestic and foreign, and depending on the appropriate mix of the two...of expanded borrowing from the World Bank," he told a news conference.
Koch-Weser said he had discussed ways the bank could help reinforce Russia's social safety net.
He added that the bank could make structural adjustment loans, similar to a $500 million credit it has agreed to help restructure the coal industry, for areas such as agriculture.

The bank agreed the coal loan, to be paid in two equal tranches, to help restructure the coal sector earlier this year but Russian officials acknowledge some regions have not made payments to mining communities agreed under the loan.

"We had very frank and productive discussions with the government of what needs to be done for us to be able to release the second tranche but I cannot elaborate as these are discussions under way," Koch-Weser said.
He said the World Bank had commitments of $6.4 billion in Russia and had paid out $2.2 billion.

Implementation of the programmes was seriously lagging earlier this year, but it had improved and disbursement was now running at $70 milion a month, instead of the $25 million a month earlier this year.
